newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle indications ranged 0.100 cent lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.
Some analysts expect further support in live cattle futures following this week's active cattle sales at higher prices. Boxed beef values also rose this week to best levels since early March.

However, others said they were thinking a top has been reached in the cash fed cattle market and prices will start to work lower as increased fed cattle supplies become available. Evening of positions ahead of the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, which will be released later Friday is also expected.

The monthly report is expected to show larger-than-year-ago on-feed supplies. Estimates for the number of cattle on feed in the seven major states in large feedlots averaged 107.6 percent of a year ago and ranged from 106 to 108 percent of last year. March 1 placements averaged 103.3 percent of a year ago and ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent and marketings averaged 100.6 percent and ranged from 98 to 104.5 percent.

Feeder cattle indications ranged mixed as near-term fundamentals point lower but longer-term factors point higher. Evening of positions ahead of the report is also expected to influence feeders, analysts said.

A lower CME feeder cattle index and higher indications on corn futures were cited as possible selling factors while the outlook for tighter feeder cattle supplies ahead was supportive. Death losses have been heavy in the Dakotas from the early April blizzard, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.11 at $70.48 per cwt.
